portfolio.core: Established brands with high share (Fevicol, Fevikwik, M-Seal): grow at 1-2x real GDP
portfolio.growth: Emerging categories (Dr. Fixit waterproofing, Roff tile adhesives, projects, joineries, WD-40, ICA wood finishes): 2-4x GDP
portfolio.pioneer: Nascent categories (Unofin renders, Haisha paints, electronics adhesives): target Rs 100 cr revenue in 3 years
portfolio.tileAdhesiveMarket: Tile & stone solutions market ~Rs 6,500 cr; penetration 20-25% (investor presentation); 25-30% (JMD, Aug-2026)

callPoints: Price increases taken across all categories (2-12% by category; blended ~4-5% mid-April plus ~7-8% early May) to offset input inflation from the West Asia conflict.
Margin helped by low-cost inventory, proactive pricing and fewer trade schemes; 'some of it will correct in the second quarter'; look at H1, not Q1 (MD and CFO).
Demand 'holding quite well'; no impact of price on demand seen yet; possible upstocking in a quarter of staggered price rises ('Perhaps yes').
VAM went from ~US$800-900/t to close to US$2,000/t and fell back; company may pass back rebates as raw materials fall.
Margin corridor of 20-24% kept; 'middle to higher end of the band' possible if crude stays mid-80s - 'big if'.
Medium-term UVG ambition double digit, 'inch it up'; real GDP 6-6.5% x category multiples gives double-digit UVG (CFO).
Competition: a large paint company built its own VAM/VAE plant; a South Indian cement maker entering tile adhesives; company says its plant network, quality and total delivered cost are its moat.
Exports fell on geopolitical issues; contracts remain and should come back as the situation normalises; some customers may have made alternate arrangements.
